## Setup

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(randomForest)
```

## Q1

```{r}

# Import and clean data
who <- read_csv("adult_census_missing.csv")
who <- na.omit(who)

# Convert categorical variables to factors
who$income <- as.factor(trimws(who$income))
who <- who %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

# Split data 80/20
set.seed(123)
index <- sample(1:nrow(who), 0.8 * nrow(who))

train <- who[index, ]
test <- who[-index, ]

# Group rare categories into "Other"
train <- train %>%
  mutate(across(
    where(is.factor) & !all_of("income"),
    ~ forcats::fct_lump_min(.x, min = 10, other_level = "Other")
  ))

# Match test categories to training categories
test <- test %>%
  mutate(across(
    where(is.factor) & !all_of("income"),
    ~ factor(
      ifelse(as.character(.x) %in% levels(train[[cur_column()]]),
             as.character(.x), "Other"),
      levels = levels(train[[cur_column()]])
    )
  ))

nrow(train)
nrow(test)
```

## Q2

```{r}

# Create decision tree
tree1 <- rpart(
  income ~ .,
  data = train,
  method = "class",
  control = rpart.control(maxdepth = 3, cp = 0.001)
)

# Predict
pred1 <- predict(tree1, test, type = "class")

# Calculate accuracy
accuracy1 <- mean(pred1 == test$income)
accuracy1

# Plot decision tree
rpart.plot(tree1)

# Plot variable importance
barplot(
  sort(tree1$variable.importance, decreasing = TRUE),
  las = 2,
  main = "Decision Tree Variable Importance"
)

```

## Q3

```{r}
# Create three additional trees
tree2 <- rpart(
  income ~ ., data = train, method = "class",
  control = rpart.control(maxdepth = 5, cp = 0.001)
)

tree3 <- rpart(
  income ~ ., data = train, method = "class",
  control = rpart.control(maxdepth = 7, cp = 0.001)
)

tree4 <- rpart(
  income ~ ., data = train, method = "class",
  control = rpart.control(maxdepth = 10, cp = 0.001)
)

# Calculate accuracy for all four trees
accuracy1 <- mean(predict(tree1, test, type = "class") == test$income)
accuracy2 <- mean(predict(tree2, test, type = "class") == test$income)
accuracy3 <- mean(predict(tree3, test, type = "class") == test$income)
accuracy4 <- mean(predict(tree4, test, type = "class") == test$income)

# Compare testing accuracy
tree_results <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Tree Depth 3", "Tree Depth 5",
            "Tree Depth 7", "Tree Depth 10"),
  Accuracy = c(accuracy1, accuracy2, accuracy3, accuracy4)
)

tree_results

# Best decision tree
tree_results[which.max(tree_results$Accuracy), ]
```

## Q4

```{r}
set.seed(123)

# Create random forest
forest1 <- randomForest(
  income ~ .,
  data = train,
  ntree = 1000,
  importance = TRUE
)

# Predict
pred_f1 <- predict(forest1, test)

# Calculate accuracy
accuracy_f1 <- mean(pred_f1 == test$income)
accuracy_f1

# Plot variable importance
varImpPlot(forest1)
```

## Q5

```{r}
set.seed(123)

# Create three additional forests
forest2 <- randomForest(
  income ~ ., data = train,
  ntree = 100, importance = TRUE
)

forest3 <- randomForest(
  income ~ ., data = train,
  ntree = 500, importance = TRUE
)

forest4 <- randomForest(
  income ~ ., data = train,
  ntree = 1500, importance = TRUE
)

# Calculate testing accuracy
accuracy_f1 <- mean(predict(forest1, test) == test$income)
accuracy_f2 <- mean(predict(forest2, test) == test$income)
accuracy_f3 <- mean(predict(forest3, test) == test$income)
accuracy_f4 <- mean(predict(forest4, test) == test$income)

# Compare random forests
forest_results <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Forest 1000", "Forest 100",
            "Forest 500", "Forest 1500"),
  Accuracy = c(accuracy_f1, accuracy_f2,
               accuracy_f3, accuracy_f4)
)

forest_results

# Best random forest
forest_results[which.max(forest_results$Accuracy), ]
```

## Q6

```{r}
# Combine all models
all_results <- rbind(tree_results, forest_results)

# Sort by testing accuracy
all_results <- all_results %>%
  arrange(desc(Accuracy))

# Display all results
all_results

# Best model
all_results[1, ]
```
